scene.label: Act 4, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Rome. Before Titus's House

content.text: Enter Young Lucius and Lavinia running after him, and the boy flies from her with his books under his arm. Enter Titus and Marcus.

lines.text: Help, grandsire, help! My aunt Lavinia
lines.plainText: Help grandsire help My aunt Lavinia

lines.text: Follows me everywhere, I know not why.
lines.plainText: Follows me everywhere I know not why

lines.text: Good uncle Marcus, see how swift she comes!
lines.plainText: Good uncle Marcus see how swift she comes

lines.text: Alas, sweet aunt, I know not what you mean.
lines.plainText: Alas sweet aunt I know not what you mean

lines.text: Stand by me, Lucius. Do not fear thine aunt.
lines.plainText: Stand by me Lucius Do not fear thine aunt

lines.text: She loves thee, boy, too well to do thee harm.
lines.plainText: She loves thee boy too well to do thee harm

lines.text: Ay, when my father was in Rome she did.
lines.plainText: Ay when my father was in Rome she did

lines.text: What means my niece Lavinia by these signs?
lines.plainText: What means my niece Lavinia by these signs

lines.text: Fear her not, Lucius. Somewhat doth she mean.
lines.plainText: Fear her not Lucius Somewhat doth she mean

lines.text: See, Lucius, see how much she makes of thee.
lines.plainText: See Lucius see how much she makes of thee

lines.text: Somewhither would she have thee go with her.
lines.plainText: Somewhither would she have thee go with her

lines.text: Ah, boy, Cornelia never with more care
lines.plainText: Ah boy Cornelia never with more care

lines.text: Read to her sons than she hath read to thee
lines.plainText: Read to her sons than she hath read to thee

lines.text: Sweet poetry and Tully's Orator.
lines.plainText: Sweet poetry and Tully's Orator

lines.text: Canst thou not guess wherefore she plies thee thus?
lines.plainText: Canst thou not guess wherefore she plies thee thus

lines.text: My lord, I know not, I, nor can I guess,
lines.plainText: My lord I know not I nor can I guess

lines.text: Unless some fit or frenzy do possess her;
lines.plainText: Unless some fit or frenzy do possess her

lines.text: For I have heard my grandsire say full oft,
lines.plainText: For I have heard my grandsire say full oft

lines.text: Extremity of griefs would make men mad;
lines.plainText: Extremity of griefs would make men mad

lines.text: And I have read that Hecuba of Troy
lines.plainText: And I have read that Hecuba of Troy

lines.text: Ran mad for sorrow. That made me to fear,
lines.plainText: Ran mad for sorrow That made me to fear

lines.text: Although, my lord, I know my noble aunt
lines.plainText: Although my lord I know my noble aunt

lines.text: Loves me as dear as e'er my mother did,
lines.plainText: Loves me as dear as e'er my mother did

lines.text: And would not, but in fury, fright my youth;
lines.plainText: And would not but in fury fright my youth

lines.text: Which made me down to throw my books, and fly,
lines.plainText: Which made me down to throw my books and fly

lines.text: Causeless, perhaps. But pardon me, sweet aunt.
lines.plainText: Causeless perhaps But pardon me sweet aunt

lines.text: And, madam, if my uncle Marcus go,
lines.plainText: And madam if my uncle Marcus go

lines.text: I will most willingly attend your ladyship.
lines.plainText: I will most willingly attend your ladyship

lines.text: Lucius, I will.
lines.plainText: Lucius I will

content.text: [Lavinia turns over with her stumps the books which Lucius has let fall.]

lines.text: How now, Lavinia? Marcus, what means this?
lines.plainText: How now Lavinia Marcus what means this

lines.text: Some book there is that she desires to see.
lines.plainText: Some book there is that she desires to see

lines.text: Which is it, girl, of these? Open them, boy.
lines.plainText: Which is it girl of these Open them boy

lines.text: But thou art deeper read and better skilled.
lines.plainText: But thou art deeper read and better skilled

lines.text: Come and take choice of all my library,
lines.plainText: Come and take choice of all my library

lines.text: And so beguile thy sorrow, till the heavens
lines.plainText: And so beguile thy sorrow till the heavens

lines.text: Reveal the damned contriver of this deed.
lines.plainText: Reveal the damned contriver of this deed

lines.text: Why lifts she up her arms in sequence thus?
lines.plainText: Why lifts she up her arms in sequence thus

lines.text: I think she means that there were more than one
lines.plainText: I think she means that there were more than one

lines.text: Confederate in the fact. Ay, more there was,
lines.plainText: Confederate in the fact Ay more there was

lines.text: Or else to heaven she heaves them for revenge.
lines.plainText: Or else to heaven she heaves them for revenge

lines.text: Lucius, what book is that she tosseth so?
lines.plainText: Lucius what book is that she tosseth so

lines.text: Grandsire, 'tis Ovid's Metamorphosis.
lines.plainText: Grandsire 'tis Ovid's Metamorphosis

lines.text: My mother gave it me.
lines.plainText: My mother gave it me

lines.text: For love of her that's gone,
lines.plainText: For love of her that's gone

lines.text: Perhaps, she culled it from among the rest.
lines.plainText: Perhaps she culled it from among the rest

lines.text: Soft! So busily she turns the leaves!
lines.plainText: Soft So busily she turns the leaves

lines.text: Help her! What would she find? Lavinia, shall I read?
lines.plainText: Help her What would she find Lavinia shall I read

lines.text: This is the tragic tale of Philomel,
lines.plainText: This is the tragic tale of Philomel

lines.text: And treats of Tereus' treason and his rape;
lines.plainText: And treats of Tereus' treason and his rape

lines.text: And rape, I fear, was root of thy annoy.
lines.plainText: And rape I fear was root of thy annoy

lines.text: See, brother, see! Note how she quotes the leaves.
lines.plainText: See brother see Note how she quotes the leaves

lines.text: Lavinia, wert thou thus surprised, sweet girl,
lines.plainText: Lavinia wert thou thus surprised sweet girl

lines.text: Ravished and wronged, as Philomela was,
lines.plainText: Ravished and wronged as Philomela was

lines.text: Forced in the ruthless, vast, and gloomy woods?
lines.plainText: Forced in the ruthless vast and gloomy woods

lines.text: See, see!
lines.plainText: See see

lines.text: Ay, such a place there is where we did hunt,—
lines.plainText: Ay such a place there is where we did hunt

lines.text: O, had we never, never hunted there!—
lines.plainText: O had we never never hunted there

lines.text: Patterned by that the poet here describes,
lines.plainText: Patterned by that the poet here describes

lines.text: By nature made for murders and for rapes.
lines.plainText: By nature made for murders and for rapes

lines.text: O, why should nature build so foul a den,
lines.plainText: O why should nature build so foul a den

lines.text: Unless the gods delight in tragedies?
lines.plainText: Unless the gods delight in tragedies

lines.text: Give signs, sweet girl, for here are none but friends,
lines.plainText: Give signs sweet girl for here are none but friends

lines.text: What Roman lord it was durst do the deed.
lines.plainText: What Roman lord it was durst do the deed

lines.text: Or slunk not Saturnine, as Tarquin erst,
lines.plainText: Or slunk not Saturnine as Tarquin erst

lines.text: That left the camp to sin in Lucrece' bed?
lines.plainText: That left the camp to sin in Lucrece' bed

lines.text: Sit down, sweet niece. Brother, sit down by me.
lines.plainText: Sit down sweet niece Brother sit down by me

lines.text: Apollo, Pallas, Jove, or Mercury,
lines.plainText: Apollo Pallas Jove or Mercury

lines.text: Inspire me, that I may this treason find!
lines.plainText: Inspire me that I may this treason find

lines.text: My lord, look here. Look here, Lavinia.
lines.plainText: My lord look here Look here Lavinia

lines.text: This sandy plot is plain; guide, if thou canst,
lines.plainText: This sandy plot is plain guide if thou canst

lines.text: This after me. I have writ my name
lines.plainText: This after me I have writ my name

content.text: [He writes his name with his staff and guides it with feet and mouth.]
[She takes the staff in her mouth, and guides it with her stumps and writes.]

lines.text: "Stuprum. Chiron. Demetrius."
lines.plainText: Stuprum Chiron Demetrius

lines.text: What, what! The lustful sons of Tamora
lines.plainText: What what The lustful sons of Tamora

lines.text: Performers of this heinous bloody deed?
lines.plainText: Performers of this heinous bloody deed

lines.text: Magni Dominator poli,
lines.plainText: Magni Dominator poli

lines.text: Tam lentus audis scelera, tam lentus vides?
lines.plainText: Tam lentus audis scelera tam lentus vides

lines.text: O, calm thee, gentle lord, although I know
lines.plainText: O calm thee gentle lord although I know

lines.text: There is enough written upon this earth
lines.plainText: There is enough written upon this earth

lines.text: To stir a mutiny in the mildest thoughts
lines.plainText: To stir a mutiny in the mildest thoughts

lines.text: And arm the minds of infants to exclaims.
lines.plainText: And arm the minds of infants to exclaims

lines.text: My lord, kneel down with me; Lavinia, kneel;
lines.plainText: My lord kneel down with me Lavinia kneel

lines.text: And kneel, sweet boy, the Roman Hector's hope;
lines.plainText: And kneel sweet boy the Roman Hector's hope

lines.text: And swear with me, as, with the woeful fere
lines.plainText: And swear with me as with the woeful fere

lines.text: And father of that chaste dishonoured dame,
lines.plainText: And father of that chaste dishonoured dame

lines.text: Lord Junius Brutus sware for Lucrece' rape,
lines.plainText: Lord Junius Brutus sware for Lucrece' rape

lines.text: That we will prosecute, by good advice
lines.plainText: That we will prosecute by good advice

lines.text: Mortal revenge upon these traitorous Goths,
lines.plainText: Mortal revenge upon these traitorous Goths

lines.text: And see their blood, or die with this reproach.
lines.plainText: And see their blood or die with this reproach

lines.text: 'Tis sure enough, an you knew how.
lines.plainText: 'Tis sure enough an you knew how

lines.text: But if you hunt these bear-whelps, then beware;
lines.plainText: But if you hunt these bearwhelps then beware

lines.text: The dam will wake, and if she wind you once.
lines.plainText: The dam will wake and if she wind you once

lines.text: She's with the lion deeply still in league,
lines.plainText: She's with the lion deeply still in league

lines.text: And lulls him whilst she playeth on her back,
lines.plainText: And lulls him whilst she playeth on her back

lines.text: And when he sleeps will she do what she list.
lines.plainText: And when he sleeps will she do what she list

lines.text: You are a young huntsman, Marcus; let alone;
lines.plainText: You are a young huntsman Marcus let alone

lines.text: And come, I will go get a leaf of brass,
lines.plainText: And come I will go get a leaf of brass

lines.text: And with a gad of steel will write these words,
lines.plainText: And with a gad of steel will write these words

lines.text: And lay it by. The angry northern wind
lines.plainText: And lay it by The angry northern wind

lines.text: Will blow these sands like Sibyl's leaves abroad,
lines.plainText: Will blow these sands like Sibyl's leaves abroad

lines.text: And where's our lesson, then? Boy, what say you?
lines.plainText: And where's our lesson then Boy what say you

lines.text: I say, my lord, that if I were a man,
lines.plainText: I say my lord that if I were a man

lines.text: Their mother's bedchamber should not be safe
lines.plainText: Their mother's bedchamber should not be safe

lines.text: For these base bondmen to the yoke of Rome.
lines.plainText: For these base bondmen to the yoke of Rome

lines.text: Ay, that's my boy! Thy father hath full oft
lines.plainText: Ay that's my boy Thy father hath full oft

lines.text: For his ungrateful country done the like.
lines.plainText: For his ungrateful country done the like

lines.text: And, uncle, so will I, an if I live.
lines.plainText: And uncle so will I an if I live

lines.text: Come, go with me into mine armoury.
lines.plainText: Come go with me into mine armoury

lines.text: Lucius, I'll fit thee; and withal, my boy,
lines.plainText: Lucius I'll fit thee and withal my boy

lines.text: Shall carry from me to the empress' sons
lines.plainText: Shall carry from me to the empress' sons

lines.text: Presents that I intend to send them both.
lines.plainText: Presents that I intend to send them both

lines.text: Come, come; thou'lt do my message, wilt thou not?
lines.plainText: Come come thou'lt do my message wilt thou not

lines.text: Ay, with my dagger in their bosoms, grandsire.
lines.plainText: Ay with my dagger in their bosoms grandsire

lines.text: No, boy, not so. I'll teach thee another course.
lines.plainText: No boy not so I'll teach thee another course

lines.text: Lavinia, come. Marcus, look to my house.
lines.plainText: Lavinia come Marcus look to my house

lines.text: Lucius and I'll go brave it at the court;
lines.plainText: Lucius and I'll go brave it at the court

lines.text: Ay, marry, will we, sir; and we'll be waited on.
lines.plainText: Ay marry will we sir and we'll be waited on

lines.text: O heavens, can you hear a good man groan
lines.plainText: O heavens can you hear a good man groan

lines.text: And not relent, or not compassion him?
lines.plainText: And not relent or not compassion him

lines.text: Marcus, attend him in his ecstasy,
lines.plainText: Marcus attend him in his ecstasy

lines.text: That hath more scars of sorrow in his heart
lines.plainText: That hath more scars of sorrow in his heart

lines.text: Than foemen's marks upon his battered shield,
lines.plainText: Than foemen's marks upon his battered shield

lines.text: But yet so just that he will not revenge.
lines.plainText: But yet so just that he will not revenge

lines.text: Revenge ye heavens for old Andronicus!
lines.plainText: Revenge ye heavens for old Andronicus
